title: Tanzanian Sukuma Wiki
community: Enjoyed nationwide — Tanzania's equivalent of Kenyan sukuma wiki
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Sukuma Wiki — collard greens sautéed with onions, tomatoes, and garlic. The most essential vegetable side dish of Tanzania — the same name and preparation shared with Kenya, reflecting the shared culinary heritage of East Africa.
longDesc: Sukuma Wiki (literally 'push the week' in Swahili — a reference to its role in stretching the week's budget) is the everyday green of Tanzania, as it is of Kenya. The Tanzanian preparation is virtually identical — simple, fast, and deeply satisfying alongside ugali.
ingredients: 500g sukuma wiki (collard greens) — washed, stems removed, thinly sliced
steps: Add sukuma wiki. Stir to combine.
Cover and cook 5—7 minutes until wilted and tender.
chefTips: Slice very thinly — thinner slices cook more evenly.
Do not add water — the leaves release sufficient moisture.
cookingScience: Collard greens contain glucosinolates — compounds that convert to isothiocyanates during chopping and mild cooking, providing cancer-protective benefits. These compounds are destroyed by overcooking.
sustainabilityTips: Sukuma wiki is one of Tanzania's most productive and affordable crops — growing year-round.
healthBenefits: Exceptionally high in vitamins A, C, and K.
culturalNote: Sukuma Wiki is shared by Tanzania and Kenya as the most important everyday green of East Africa — the name in Swahili captures its role perfectly: 'push the week' — the vegetable that makes a modest budget stretch to feed a family.
